analyst_view.overall: Lyon (4th, 20 points) host Monaco (8th, 17 points) on Sunday evening, three days after both played in Europe: Lyon drew 0-0 at home to Lillestrom with a rotated side, Monaco won 3-2 at Hearts with a late Balogun goal, their first win in seven games. Carlos Vicens' Lyon miss Sulc, Morton and Ouedraogo for months, with Bidstrup and Mata doubtful, but striker Loic Openda is back after two months out and played the last minutes on Thursday. Filipe Luis' Monaco lose Mamadou Coulibaly to suspension and are without Golovin, Ansu Fati and Idumbo, with Paris Brunner doubtful or out and Salisu doubtful; the numbers now count these absences, so my earlier cut for them is dropped. Jerome Brisard referees (4.1 cards a game, already counted); Monaco have won three of the last five meetings.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals, 1.4 for Lyon, and they now take off Sulc, Bidstrup, Brunner, Golovin, Idumbo and Coulibaly. Lyon's four goals in six came largely without Openda, who is back and projected to start by one preview, and Monaco's high press under Filipe Luis has been leaking long-range goals, so I lean a little higher, 2.3 to about 2.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, already raised for Lyon's 38 corners in their last six. Both sides play wide (Lyon with Nuamah and Nakamura, Monaco with wing-backs Vanderson and Nazinho), which their ratings already know, so I stay at about 10.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards, raised about 7% for referee Jerome Brisard (4.1 a game over 51 games, his 26th Lyon match) and trimmed because both sides have been booked less than usual lately. There is no rivalry or discipline news, so I stay at about 4.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.3 shots. Lyon rested several starters on Thursday while Monaco played their first team away at Hearts, which may help Lyon's energy a little, but Monaco's pressing style already shows in their figures, so I stay at about 25.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target, fairly even between the sides. Openda's return could sharpen Lyon slightly, but he has played only a few minutes in two months and Balogun leads Monaco's line as usual, so I stay at about 9.
